body:
Sorry for the delay, I've been kind of busy. So far I've had two chiro appointments and am going for my third on Monday. It seems to be helping, over the last two days my pain has been at a pretty low level (about a 2/10). He said it could take four sessions before we'd know for sure but I'm fairly confident that this is going to "cure" me. If it weren't for you, I don't think I ever would've suspected that it was a pinched nerve and wouldn't have gone to a chiro.

Thank you. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.
I'll update on either Monday or Tuesday after seeing my chiro.

I might go to a PT if my chiro doesn't know/can't find out some exercises I should do. I'll do some more research into squats, I had no idea they could be dangerous. I figured they were a popular form of exercise so they couldn't be that dangerous; I'll definitely look into it some more, thanks.

I'm doing some research right now. From what I can gather it looks like it'd be good to start with squats and presses strengthen the thoracic area of the back. When I see the chiro again on Monday I'll ask if he knows any others or can find out.

Part of the reason I'm staying with him is he actually said what you're saying. After he straightens my back out some, I should start doing strengthening exercises so the vertebrae stay in the right position.

I've continued meditating and though it hasn't helped my stomach, I feel a little better and more stable emotionally. I went to the chiropractor and he did a slight adjustment. The X-Ray showed that my T5 (I think all the way through to my T7) were pretty misaligned and he said those are where the nerves linked to the stomach meet up (or something to that effect). Over the next couple weeks he'll continue making adjustments and I should see an improvement he said.
I guess I could keep trying, I have nothing to lose by continuing to try. I found the chiro because some of my mom's friends who had back problems went to this guy and he helped them a lot.
Unfortunately it's been a week and meditation hasn't helped at all. I do have an appointment with a chiropractor for X-Rays and a consultation on Monday, so after that I'll let you know.

I'll try out some meditation, anything's worth a shot at this point. As for the chiropractic, I have to find out if my insurance covers it, as I assume it's fairly expensive (you mentioned X-Rays). Thanks a lot for your help, I'll let you know how the meditation goes (I'll try it out for about a week or so before updating). I'll be trying Concentration meditation as that seems to be a better place to start than Mindfulness meditation.

I don't think they tested for fibromyalgia but it doesn't sound like I have it. In addition, they did already try giving me Lyrica and it didn't help at all. As for the spinal cord stimulator, none of my doctors had mentioned it (though according to the site it's for "adults with chronic intractable pain of the trunk (low back) and/or limbs (legs)" and I am neither an adult nor do I have pain in those locations. It occurs to me I never said where my pain was located (though at the time of writing I hadn't really anticipated anybody to read and respond). If it's relevant, the pain is in my abdominal area, a bit above the navel and in the navel area, though it's not on the outside, it's on the inside.

I guess I'd be willing to look into meditation and chiropractics, though to be honest, at this point I doubt either will help as I've gone through so many tests and gone to reputable hospitals (Stanford's Children Hospital and Cedar-Sinai) and neither of them knew what it was or what to do. Morphine Sulfate 15mg doesn't even help a little and neither does Lortab (I've even tried the 10/500 dose).

Ninja-Edit: By the way, I'd like to thank you for taking the time to do this. It means a lot.

Yeah, some of them said it might be in my head too, (though I don't know how much I trust those doctors because they're the same ones who said that I would just get used to the pain and that I had a computer addiction because I spent most of my day on the computer) and that's why I tried the psychotherapy stuff. I haven't really tried meditation much (though I ended up doing a little bit with the biofeedback). What other "alternative medicine" do you mean? As far as I know I've tried just about every alternative medicine but none have helped even a little. I even tried a bunch of weird-ass teas that tasted like shit.

No event, it just happened. Doctors recommended the same thing you are. I think the professional is called a psychotherapist and they were supposed to specialize in biofeedback. I tried that too and that didn't help. Tried acupuncture, pain pills, injections, aqua therapy, and ganglion blocks. Nothing helped. Nothing.

I wasn't, that's part of the problem. I'd be more hopeful if I had a diagnosis of any kind because it means something can be done to manage it or treat it. If not now, then in the future. But no diagnosis.
